scope: Proposition 7.1 (Finite form structure) of the manuscript “Constant-factor hardness of uniform sparsest cut” (preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026/Constant-factor-hardness-of-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 117 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 75f6af00a38589bf), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The demand law and the raw comparison measures in Theorem 6.1 have polynomially enumerable discrete seeds, whose positive probabilities are bounded below by an inverse polynomial in input size. For each seed, after finitely many fixed subdivisions of numerical boxes, their conditional densities are nonnegative rational polynomials and the score table entries are rational polynomials of bounded degree in a fixed number of numerical variables. There are only finitely many such numerical polynomial patterns, independent of input size. The total raw comparison mass is finite and bounded by a constant. For any fixed finite grid and deterministic entrywise rounding rule, every positive rounded demand mass or comparison-pair mass has an inverse-polynomial lower bound.
